newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, U.S., UK repel mock attack close to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, U.S., UK repel mock attack close to Iraq.

text.p: Kuwaiti warplanes backed by American tanks and British infantry on Wednesday repelled a mock enemy attack near the Iraqi border.

The 1991 Gulf War coalition forces that drove Iraq from Kuwait "are still here and our relationship and training is improving," Kuwait's armed forces chief of staff General Ali al-Mo'men told reporters.

"I hope he (Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein) gets the message that we have a deterrent here which he needs to take into consideration," added Mo'men after U.S. M1A1 tanks and Kuwaiti F/A-18 jets pounded Iraqi tanks already destroyed during the war.
Wednesday's live fire exercise, 40 km (25 miles) south of the Iraqi border, was the climax of the U.S.-led Intrinsic Action 96 manoeuvre which started in August and is due to end by mid-December.
A hundred Cyprus-based British infantry joined their Kuwaiti counterparts in repelling the attack, firing automatic weapons at pop up enemy cut outs.

In September Washington ordered a huge military buildup in the oil-rich Gulf to deter what it called renewed Iraqi threats, sending more than 3,000 ground troops to Kuwait in addition to 1,200 already in the tiny state.

Commander of Task Force-Kuwait, Major-General Robert Ivany, told Reuters "Right now we have no (firm) deployment dates at all and will continue to train in the desert. These forces will continue to stay here in the desert."
The chief of staff of U.S. troops in Kuwait, Colonel Robert Pollard, told Reuters "Iraq has a lot of combat power up there...They are only 70 miles (112 km) from Kuwait City."
